'''Maxwell Alexander Rosenlicht''' (April 15, 1924 – January 22, 1999) was an American [[mathematician]] known for works in [[algebraic geometry]], [[algebraic group]]s, and [[differential algebra]].

Rosenlicht attended high school in Brooklyn ([[Erasmus Hall High School|Erasmus High School]]) and studied at [[Columbia University]] (B.A. 1947) and at Harvard University, where he worked under [[Oscar Zariski|Zariski]]. He was a [[Putnam fellow]] twice, in 1946 and 1947.<ref name="MMA">{{cite web |title=Putnam Competition Individual and Team Winners |url=http://www.maa.org/programs/maa-awards/putnam-competition-individual-and-team-winners |publisher=[[Mathematical Association of America]] |access-date=December 10, 2021 |archive-date=March 12, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140312205244/http://www.maa.org/programs/maa-awards/putnam-competition-individual-and-team-winners |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was awarded his doctorate on algebraic curve equivalence concepts in 1950. In 1952, he moved to [[Northwestern University]]. From 1958 until his retirement in 1991, he was a professor at the University of California, Berkeley. He was also a visiting professor in Mexico City, [[Institut des Hautes Études Scientifiques|IHÉS]], Rome, Leiden, and at Harvard University.

In 1960, he shared the [[Cole Prize]] in algebra with [[Serge Lang]] for his work on [[Generalized Jacobian variety|generalized Jacobian varieties]].<ref>{{Cite journal |title=Generalized Jacobian varieties |journal=[[Annals of Mathematics]] |volume=59 |year=1954 |pages=505–530 |doi= 10.2307/1969715|jstor=1969715 |last1=Rosenlicht |first1=Maxwell |issue=3 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |title=A universal mapping property of generalized Jacobians |journal=Annals of Mathematics |volume=66 |issue=1 |year=1957 |pages=80–88 |doi= 10.2307/1970118 |jstor=1970118 |last1=Rosenlicht |first1=Maxwell }}</ref> He also studied the algorithmic algebraic theory of integration.

Rosenlicht was a Fulbright Fellow and 1954 Guggenheim Fellow.

He died of neurological disease on a trip to Hawaii. Rosenlicht married in 1954 and had four children.
